content: # Learning History ## Current Learning Goals I am currently expanding beyond my existing software engineering experience into: * Artificial Intelligence * Generative AI * Large Language Models * RAG * AI Agents * Machine Learning * Data Engineering * AI application development * System Design My goal is not just to use AI tools. I want to understand how AI-powered applications are designed, implemented, integrated, and deployed end-to-end. --- ## Python ### Current Level I have Python fundamentals and am actively improving my practical Python skills. ### Topics * Python fundamentals * NumPy * Pandas * Data manipulation * Machine learning implementation * APIs * FastAPI ### Areas to Continue Improving * Advanced Python * Writing clean production-quality Python * Object-oriented programming * Error handling * Testing * Performance * Python for AI/ML applications --- ## NumPy ### Topics Studied * NumPy arrays * Array operations * `np.random.seed()` * Minimum and maximum operations * Axis * Normalization * Broadcasting fundamentals ### Important Learning Notes `np.random.seed()` controls the starting point of NumPy's pseudo-random number generation so that random results can be reproduced. For example: ```python np.random.seed(42) ``` The number `42` is not special. Another integer can be used. --- ## Machine Learning ### Current Learning Stage I am learning Machine Learning fundamentals progressively through practical exercises. ### Topics * NumPy for ML * Data preprocessing * Normalization * Linear Regression * Training models * Features and targets * Model fitting * Predictions * Understanding errors and debugging ### Current Goal Understand ML concepts through implementation rather than only theoretical study. --- ## AI / Generative AI ### Current Interest I want to learn how real-world AI applications are built rather than only learning how to prompt existing AI models. ### Topics I Want to Learn * LLM APIs * Prompt engineering * Context management * Structured outputs * Embeddings * Vector databases * RAG * Long-term memory * Episodic memory * Tool calling * Function calling * AI agents * Agent orchestration * Evaluation * AI application architecture * Deployment * Production AI systems --- ## Databricks / AI I have been exploring Databricks Genie and how it fits into AI-powered applications. Topics of interest: * Databricks Genie * LLM-powered data interaction * Chatbot architecture * Genie vs traditional chatbot architectures * Backend integration * AI agents * Data-aware AI applications --- ## Current Personal AI Project I am currently building a Personal AI Assistant. ### What I Want to Learn Through It * How an LLM API works. * How to build a chatbot from scratch. * How to provide an LLM with personal context. * How RAG works. * How embeddings work. * How vector databases work. * How memory should be designed. * How tool calling works. * How agents work. * How to connect a frontend to an AI backend. * How to deploy an AI application publicly. * How to secure API keys. * How to structure an AI application for future expansion. ### Current Project Stage V1: * Python * Streamlit * LLM API * Personal knowledge files * Basic chatbot Planned: V2: * RAG * Embeddings * Vector database V3: * Persistent memory * Interview memory * Learning memory V4: * Tools * Web search * Agentic workflows V5: * Advanced Personal AI Assistant --- ## Learning Philosophy I learn best by building practical projects. I should avoid spending excessive time learning frameworks without understanding the underlying concepts. For AI projects, I want to understand the underlying architecture before relying heavily on abstractions or frameworks. When learning a new concept, I should preferably: 1. Understand the problem. 2. Build a simple version. 3. Understand why it works. 4. Experiment with it. 5. Then introduce frameworks or more advanced implementations. --- ## Learning Weaknesses This section should be updated over time based on my actual performance. Current known gaps should not be assumed unless I explicitly identify them. The Personal AI should detect recurring weaknesses from my conversations, coding exercises, interview performance, and learning history. --- ## Future Learning Log For every significant learning session, record: Date: Topic: What I learned: What I implemented: What I understood well: What I struggled with: Questions I still have: Next topic: Confidence: The Personal AI should use this history to recommend what I should learn next rather than repeatedly suggesting generic learning roadmaps.

# Interview History and Preparation ## Purpose This file stores information about my interviews, questions I was asked, areas where I performed well, areas where I struggled, and topics that I should improve. The Personal AI should use this information to identify recurring weaknesses and personalize future interview preparation. ## Historical Interviews Detailed historical interview information has not yet been documented. When I provide interview information, record it using the following structure. --- ## Interview Template ### Interview Company: Role: Date: Interview Round: Interview Type: ### Questions Asked 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. ### Questions I Answered Well * ### Questions I Struggled With * ### Questions I Could Not Answer * ### Technical Topics Covered * ### Non-Technical Topics Covered * ### Feedback Received * ### My Own Assessment What went well: What went poorly: What I should improve: ### Follow-Up Learning Topics I need to revise: 1. 2. 3. ### Personal AI Assessment After every interview, the Personal AI should analyze the interview and identify: * Repeatedly asked topics. * Topics I struggle with. * Topics where my answers are strong. * Technical gaps. * Communication gaps. * Missing project details. * Questions I should practice again. * Topics likely to appear in future interviews. --- ## Interview Preparation Goals The Personal AI should help me prepare for interviews based on: * My resume. * My actual projects. * My technical skills. * My previous interviews. * My weak areas. * The job description. * The target role. * My career goals. It should avoid giving generic interview preparation whenever enough personal context is available. For example, instead of simply asking: "What are common Python interview questions?" it should consider my current experience and ask questions relevant to my actual background. --- ## Important Interview Context My strongest professional experience currently includes: * Angular * .NET * FastAPI * Azure * Azure DevOps * CI/CD * REST APIs * SignalR * WebSockets * SQL * Microsoft 365 integrations * Full-stack application development * Internal application development * Technical leadership Areas I am currently interested in developing further include: * AI * Generative AI * LLM applications * RAG * AI agents * Machine Learning * Data Engineering * System Design --- ## Future Interview Memory Whenever I discuss an interview with my Personal AI, it should remember useful information such as: * Questions I struggled with. * Questions I answered well. * Concepts I misunderstood. * Concepts I need to revise. * Interviewer feedback. * My confidence level. * Repeated weaknesses. * Improvements between interviews. This information should influence future interview preparation.

# Projects ## 1. SIMOPs Schedule Optimizer ### Overview A real-time operations platform focused on schedule optimization, conflict detection, and geospatial visualization. ### Technologies Angular .NET SignalR Azure Leaflet.js Turf.js NetTopologySuite Microsoft Identity Platform JWT Google OR-Tools Azure Data Lake Azure SQL Azure Data Factory ### What I Worked On * Real-time schedule and conflict updates using SignalR. * Interactive geospatial visualization. * Conflict analysis for well trajectories, pad boundaries, and conflict zones. * Secure authentication using JWT and Microsoft Identity Platform. * Scheduling optimization using Google OR-Tools. * Data ingestion and processing using Azure Data Lake, Azure SQL, and Azure Data Factory. * Full-stack application development and production delivery. ### Impact * Reduced manual review effort by 50%+. * Enabled early detection of high-impact conflicts. * Reported savings of $5M per incident. ### Interview Talking Points Potential areas to discuss: * Why SignalR was required. * How real-time updates were implemented. * How geospatial data was visualized. * How conflict detection works. * Why Google OR-Tools was used. * Authentication architecture. * Azure architecture. * Data ingestion flow. * Performance and scalability. * Challenges faced during development. --- ## 2. Enterprise Workforce Automation Platform ### Overview An internal employee lifecycle management platform designed to automate manual processes and improve operational efficiency. ### Technologies Angular .NET Azure Azure AD MSAL JWT Microsoft 365 SharePoint Teams Chart.js Azure DevOps ### What I Worked On * Proposed and led development of the application. * Employee lifecycle management. * Document management. * Workflow automation. * Operational dashboards. * Role-based access control. * Azure AD/MSAL/JWT authentication. * Microsoft 365 integrations. * CI/CD pipelines. * Multi-environment deployments. * Configuration and monitoring. ### Impact * Adopted across multiple accounts. * Reduced administrative overhead by 70%. * Eliminated several manual processes. ### Interview Talking Points Potential areas to discuss: * Why the application was needed. * Authentication and authorization architecture. * Role-based access control. * Microsoft 365 integration. * Workflow architecture. * Angular/.NET communication. * CI/CD design. * Multi-environment configuration. * Deployment strategy. * Challenges and trade-offs. --- ## 3. Centralized Reporting & Review System ### Overview A full-stack reporting platform for creating, validating, reviewing, and approving regulatory and business reports. ### Technologies Angular FastAPI Figma WebSockets ### What I Worked On * Report creation. * Report validation. * Approval workflows. * Automated commentary generation. * Role-based review workflows. * Real-time functionality using WebSockets. * Chatbot-style support. * Full-stack development. ### Impact * Reduced reporting cycle time by 40%. * Improved accuracy by 25%. * Reduced manual input by 60%. * Reduced approval turnaround time by 30%. ### Interview Talking Points Potential areas to discuss: * Why FastAPI was selected. * Angular/FastAPI architecture. * WebSocket implementation. * Real-time communication. * Automated commentary generation. * Role-based workflows. * Report validation. * Chatbot-style functionality. * Performance considerations. --- ## 4. Personal AI Assistant ### Status Currently being built. ### Goal Build a personal AI assistant that understands my professional, learning, project, and interview context. ### Core Capabilities Planned * Personal profile knowledge. * Resume knowledge. * Project knowledge. * Interview history. * Learning history. * Persistent memory. * RAG. * LLM-powered conversations. * Personalized interview preparation. * Career assistance. * Job description analysis. * Learning recommendations. * Technical question answering. * Project context retrieval. ### Planned Architecture User ↓ Chat UI ↓ Python application ↓ Memory / Knowledge Retrieval ↓ LLM ↓ Personalized response ### Future Capabilities * Embeddings. * Vector database. * Long-term memory. * Episodic memory. * Tool calling. * Web search. * Agentic workflows. * Interview evaluation. * Career analysis. * Personalized daily recommendations. ### Main Learning Goals This project is intended to help me understand: * LLM APIs. * Prompt engineering. * RAG. * Embeddings. * Vector databases. * Memory architecture. * Structured outputs. * Tool calling. * AI agents. * Backend architecture. * Frontend integration. * Deployment. * Production considerations.

I have also led the Software Engineering Council of 40+ engineers, helping standardize Angular, .NET, and FastAPI engineering practices across multiple teams. ## Technical Skills ### Languages * TypeScript * C# * Python * SQL ### Frontend * Angular * RxJS * HTML * CSS * SCSS * Chart.js * Leaflet.js ### Backend * .NET * ASP.NET Core * Entity Framework Core * ADO.NET * FastAPI * REST APIs * SignalR * WebSockets ### Databases and Data * SQL Server * Azure SQL * Azure Data Lake * Azure Data Factory ### Cloud and DevOps * Microsoft Azure * Azure DevOps * CI/CD * YAML * Azure App Services ### Tools and Integrations * Git * Microsoft Graph * Power BI * Figma * Microsoft 365 integrations ## Professional Strengths * Full-stack application development * Backend API development * Frontend development * Cloud deployment * CI/CD pipeline implementation * Real-time application development * Authentication and authorization * Workflow automation * Data processing and integration * Internal tool development * Technical leadership * Cross-team engineering standardization * Problem solving * Reducing manual operational effort ## Career Goals I want to continue growing as a strong software engineer while developing deeper expertise in: * Artificial Intelligence * Generative AI * LLM applications * RAG * AI agents * AI application architecture * Machine Learning * Data Engineering * Cloud * System Design I want to move beyond simply using AI tools and understand how to design, build, deploy, and maintain real AI-powered applications. ## Current Personal AI Project I am currently building a personal AI assistant for myself.
